title: Made VFX for my deckbuilder with video models — hit effects, status effects, buffs
author: Joeykiwis
selftext:
My last post about the videos I made with MiniMax-H3 got a really good response, so I figured I should lean on image and video generation more in my game dev.

Lately I've been making VFX using video models.

My game is a deckbuilding card game, and up until now there weren't many effects when you played a card — it felt kind of dull.

So I started with hit effects for each class, magic bolt effects, and so on.

[VFX only ](https://reddit.com/link/1w0mi08/video/s2z7x4cza3mh1/player)

The monsters are random picks from the game's 5 stages.

[VFX on monster](https://reddit.com/link/1w0mi08/video/yjunfi42b3mh1/player)

  
And with status effects, even when one got applied, nothing was really visible on the monster other than the status icon — same with buffs. Once I added VFX, it read a lot better.

So here's a first batch of VFX I've made.

https://i.redd.it/zten8r4sb3mh1.gif

Just in case — I'm making a game where the orcs are the player characters.

Which means the orcs with VFX on them in the last clip aren't monsters!

They're the heroes!



This is my first time making VFX, so I know there's a lot that's lacking.

Open to feedback — please share your thoughts.

comments.author: Lavio00
comments.body: How the f..? You used minmax to create vfx? You’re a genius! How did you prompt it?

replies.author: Joeykiwis
replies.body:
I give Claude Code a VFX reference image and tell it to have H3 generate the VFX from that. I develop this way, so I don't actually know every prompt myself. Just asked it what it used, so here you go lol

It's two stages — Z-Image for the shape, then H3 for the motion.

**Block**

Shape: \`A round orc war shield seen face on, thick weathered wooden planks with visible grain, a ring of iron studs around the rim and a heavy metal boss in the centre, grey iron tones with pale highlights and dark outline.\`

Motion: \`the shield breaks apart into wooden chunks that drift away\`

Played in reverse, so the chunks pull together into a shield.

**Strength**

Shape: \`A flexed green orc arm like the strong arm emoji, bent at the elbow with the fist at the top, a huge bulging bicep, a white bandage strip wrapped around the wrist, thick black outline.\`

Motion: \`the arm flexes and the bicep bulges bigger\`
